title: Reflect fully, then choose
hookLine: the handoff: the plan is tidy, and the next person might change half of it
carry: the teaching ends with a choice, not an order
tomorrow: why would God want to know what loving God feels like?

lines: I MIGHT CHANGE SOME OF THIS.
cards: The handoff doc is finished. The notes are tidy, every reason written down. Then the person taking over reads it and says, thanks, I might change some of this.
There's a word on the tip of the tongue, and it's: don't. The Bhagavad Gita ends near a moment a lot like that. Between two armies, Krishna has taught Arjuna for chapters and made his whole case.
And then he hands Arjuna something a reader might not expect from a teacher who's just won the argument.

teach.h: REFLECT FULLY, THEN DO AS YOU WISH.
teach.b: Near the end, Krishna says, in paraphrase: I've told you this wisdom, more secret than any secret. Reflect on it fully. Then do as you wish.
No order. The choice, handed back.
Arjuna's answer comes a few verses later: my confusion is gone, my memory has come back, I stand firm, my doubts are gone, and I'll do as you say. Notice the order.
Reflection first, then a free yes. A yes that was ordered wouldn't be the same yes. That's the capstone's last move, and not an easy one.
A year of service, designed and reviewed, ends by being handed on. The designer explains the reasons fully: why the pace is measured, why the gifts are quiet, why the review asks about others.
Then lets the next person choose. Some of the plan will change. The teacher in the Gita seems to take that risk on purpose, because what he's after isn't obedience.
That's a deep thread in Hindu teaching: dharma is meant to be understood, not just obeyed, and the Gita itself ends by handing the choice back.

Readers hear the verse in more than one way: some as real freedom given to Arjuna, some as a teacher's trust that full reflection will lead one way. Both keep the same order. Think it through, then choose.
And the capstone comes full circle. It began with the work already on the calendar. It ends with the work in someone else's hands.

how: Some Hindu teachers point to Gita 18.63 when they speak of teaching: the student is given reasons and asked to reflect, and the choice is left to them.

o: action that must never change once planned
action explained fully, then handed on freely
action done only because an order was given

p: reflect fully, then do as you wish
confusion gone; I'll do as you say
not the same as a free yes
explain fully, then hand it on

s: in the Gita, Krishna wants obedience without reflection
near the end he says: reflect on all of this fully, then do as you wish.
Arjuna answers that his confusion is gone and he'll do as Krishna says
reflection first, then a free yes.
handing on a plan well means giving no reasons
Krishna explains fully first; the choice comes after the reasons.

games.q: you're teaching your little brother a family recipe, and he wants to add chili to it. what does Gita 18.63 suggest?
o: tell him why it's made this way, then let him decide.
forbid it. a recipe handed down shouldn't change.
let him do anything, and skip the explaining.
games.why: Krishna gives his reasons in full, then says: do as you wish. the free yes, or the free change, comes after understanding.

practice: Close your eyes if that's comfortable. Bring to mind one thing you're about to pass on: a job, a habit, a recipe, a piece of advice.
On each out-breath, loosen your grip on how it has to turn out, and rest in having explained it well.

wordCard.voice: Karma, handed on: work explained fully, then given over to someone else's free choice.

orig.note: Sanskrit, from Gita 18.63: as you wish, so do. Krishna's words after reflect on it fully.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: the Gita's teaching ends with a choice, not an order. The capstone is complete.

sources.ref: Bhagavad Gita 18.63 (thus I have told you wisdom more secret than the secret; reflect on it fully, then do as you wish)
Bhagavad Gita 18.73 (Arjuna: my delusion is gone, memory regained, I stand firm, my doubts gone, I will do your word)
